stem: A mutation converts the start codon ATG to ATC. The most likely consequence is:

options.A: Translation begins at a different codon
options.B: The first amino acid is valine instead of methionine
options.C: Translation does not initiate; no protein is made
options.D: The mRNA is degraded before translation

stem: In heterozygote advantage, the heterozygote HbAS shows a survival benefit under malaria-endemic conditions because:

options.A: The heterozygote is homozygous normal and immune to malaria
options.B: The heterozygote produces two types of hemoglobin, both beneficial
options.C: One sickle allele provides malaria resistance without severe disease
options.D: Heterozygotes have higher oxygen-binding capacity than homozygotes

stem: A CRISPR edit corrects the sickle cell mutation (HBB GAG to GTG) in a diploid embryo. The phenotype of the edited embryo will be:

options.A: Sickle cell disease (if the other allele is also sickle)
options.B: Normal or carrier phenotype (depends on the other HBB allele)
options.C: Enhanced EPO expression and improved oxygen delivery
options.D: Identical to the parents because germline edits revert by adulthood

A team uses PGT to select an embryo with the highest predicted EPO expression. This approach works because:

options.A: The EPO gene is easily edited in embryos
options.B: Embryos with different allelic variants at the EPO locus show different phenotypes
options.C: PGT can predict future environmental effects on EPO

stem: A cell with impaired hemoglobin function will show reduced ATP production because:

options.A: ATP is made only in the nucleus
options.B: Hemoglobin delivers oxygen to mitochondria, enabling aerobic respiration
options.C: Hemoglobin is required for glycolysis to occur
options.D: ATP production is independent of oxygen availability
